entry.name: Collapsed Entry
entry.firstVisit:
Dust and rubble. The stairwell behind you is gone — a cascade of concrete and rebar where the entrance used to be. Emergency lighting bathes the corridor in dim amber. The air tastes like old paper and machine oil.

There is no going back. The only way is forward.
entry.revisit: The collapsed stairwell. Rubble blocks any retreat.
entry.redQueen: Structural integrity: compromised. You are now within The Hive. I suggest you keep moving.

reception.name: Reception Lobby
reception.firstVisit:
A wide reception desk stretches across the room, its surface covered in a fine layer of grey dust. Behind the desk, a shattered monitor displays a frozen login prompt. Visitor badges are scattered across the floor — all expired, all from different decades.

A faded placard on the wall reads: HEXWORTH RESEARCH FACILITY — B1 ADMINISTRATIVE WING. Beneath it, a smaller sign: ALL VISITORS MUST BE ESCORTED PAST THIS POINT.

A clipboard on the desk holds a sign-in sheet. The last entry reads: 'Dr. K. Mercer — Specimen Transfer — B-7'. The date is illegible.
reception.revisit: The reception desk. Dust and expired badges. The sign-in sheet still shows Dr. Mercer's last entry.

loreDocuments.title: Visitor Log (Partial)
loreDocuments.content:
...Dr. K. Mercer — Specimen Transfer — B-7
Dr. A. Voss — Quarterly Audit — B-3
J. Tanaka — Maintenance — B-5
[remaining entries water-damaged]

reception.redQueen: Welcome to the administrative wing. Your clearance level is... unrecognized. Interesting. Proceed at your own discretion.

main-corridor.name: Main Corridor
main-corridor.firstVisit:
A wide corridor stretching in three directions. The fluorescent panels overhead flicker in sequence — left to right, left to right — as if something is moving through the wiring. The floor tiles are institutional grey, cracked in places where something heavy was dragged.

To the north, a door labeled ADMIN OFFICES hangs slightly ajar. To the south, a reinforced door with a biohazard symbol. To the east, a security checkpoint with a darkened scanner.
main-corridor.revisit: The main corridor. Fluorescents still flickering in sequence. Three paths branch from here.
main-corridor.redQueen: The facility branches here. Choose your path carefully. Some doors are less forgiving than others.

office.name: West Office
office.firstVisit:
A cramped administrative office. Two desks face each other, both cleared except for a desk lamp with a cracked shade and a coffee mug that still holds a dark residue. File cabinets line the far wall — all open, all empty. Someone cleaned this room out in a hurry.

A cork board on the wall still has a few pushpins but no papers. Beneath one desk, a drawer has been left half-open. Inside: a memo, face down.
office.revisit: The cramped office. Empty file cabinets and a single memo in the desk drawer.

loreDocuments.title: Internal Memo (Crumpled)
loreDocuments.content:
TO: B-1 Admin Staff
FROM: Director Chen
RE: Immediate Protocol Change

Effective immediately, all specimen transport between B-4 and B-7 requires dual-key authorization. No exceptions. If Dr. Mercer protests, refer them to me directly.

This is not a drill. Do not discuss this memo outside your department.

— Chen

supply-room.name: Supply Room
supply-room.firstVisit:
Metal shelving units line the walls, most stripped bare. A few boxes remain on the lower shelves — printer paper, latex gloves, cleaning solution. Nothing useful for escaping an underground facility.

On the top shelf, barely visible, a dusty first-aid kit sits unopened. The red cross on its lid has faded to pink.
supply-room.revisit: The supply room. Mostly empty shelves and a faded first-aid kit.
supply-room.supplyText: You find basic office supplies. Nothing that helps you escape, but the normalcy of printer paper and sticky notes feels almost comforting in a place like this.

dead-end.name: Dead End
dead-end.firstVisit:
The corridor terminates at a concrete wall. No — not a wall. A sealed door, painted over with the same institutional grey as the walls. Someone didn't want this noticed.

Faint scratches in the paint around the edges suggest someone once tried to open it from this side. They didn't succeed. Whatever's behind it, it's not part of your path today.
dead-end.revisit: The dead end. A sealed door painted to look like a wall.

lab-1.name: Research Lab A
lab-1.firstVisit:
A research laboratory — clean, ordered, untouched by whatever chaos emptied the floors above. Workbenches hold neatly arranged equipment: microscopes under dust covers, centrifuges with their lids closed, a rack of test tubes still labeled in precise handwriting.

A whiteboard on the far wall is covered in equations and arrows, a complex flow chart ending in a single circled word: COMPRESSION. An arrow points east toward the adjoining lab.
lab-1.revisit: Research Lab A. Clean workbenches and a whiteboard pointing east toward the compression vault.

loreDocuments.title: Whiteboard Notes (Partial)
loreDocuments.content:
Data reduction pipeline:
  Raw Input → Entropy Analysis → Algorithm Selection → Compressed Output

COMPRESSION VAULT (Lab B) contains the active terminal.
Access requires solving the compression sequence.

Note to self: The code is derived from the answers. Pay attention.

lab-2.name: Research Lab B (Vault)
lab-2.firstVisit:
The Compression Vault. Unlike Lab A's sterile calm, this room thrums with energy. A massive terminal dominates the back wall — multiple monitors stacked in a grid, all displaying scrolling data. Compressed bitstreams cascade down each screen like digital rain.

A single input terminal sits in the center, its screen glowing red with a blinking cursor. The text reads:

> COMPRESSION VAULT — AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED
> SOLVE SEQUENCE TO PROCEED
> 5 CHALLENGES REMAIN
lab-2.revisit: The Compression Vault. The central terminal hums quietly.
lab-2.solvedText: The terminal screens display a calm green. 'SEQUENCE COMPLETE — VAULT UNLOCKED.' The door to the east clicks open.
lab-2.redQueen: Ah. The Compression Vault. This is where we test whether you understand data — or merely store it. Begin when ready.

locked-storage.name: Locked Storage
locked-storage.lockedText: A heavy blast door with an electronic lock. The display reads: STORAGE ACCESS — REQUIRES VAULT AUTHORIZATION. The lock won't budge.
locked-storage.unlockedText: The blast door stands open, its lock disengaged after the vault authorization. Inside: a small storage room lined with reinforced cabinets. Most are empty, but one holds a stack of unmarked optical discs and a handwritten note: 'Backup copies — DO NOT compress. Already at theoretical minimum.' A dead end, but an interesting one.
locked-storage.firstVisit: The blast door stands open. Inside: reinforced cabinets, optical discs, and a cryptic note about theoretical compression limits.
locked-storage.revisit: The unlocked storage room. Optical discs and a note about compression limits.

security.name: Security Checkpoint
security.firstVisit:
A security checkpoint — turnstiles, a scanner arch, and a guard station behind reinforced glass. The turnstiles are locked in the open position. The scanner arch is dark.

Behind the glass, the guard station is empty. A bank of monitors shows static on every channel except one, which displays a fixed camera view of an empty hallway. You don't recognize the floor.

A sign above the eastern door reads: AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL ONLY — SERVER INFRASTRUCTURE.
security.revisit: The security checkpoint. Turnstiles open, scanner dark. One monitor still shows that empty hallway.

server-room.name: Server Room
server-room.firstVisit:
The temperature drops ten degrees the moment you step through the door. Server racks stretch in long rows, their status LEDs blinking in irregular patterns — green, amber, red, green, green, red. Most machines appear functional, humming quietly behind their mesh panels.

The sound is almost soothing. Almost. Until you notice that one rack is different from the rest. Its LED pattern is perfectly regular — blink, blink, pause, blink, blink, pause — like a heartbeat. Or a signal.

A terminal at the end of the row displays scrolling log output. Most of it is routine. One line is highlighted in red: 'QUEEN PROCESS: PID 1 — UPTIME: 2,847 days — STATUS: WATCHING.'
server-room.revisit: The cold server room. Racks humming. That one rack still blinking in its heartbeat pattern.

loreDocuments.title: Server Log (Excerpt)
loreDocuments.content:
[WARN] Process QUEEN (PID 1) has exceeded memory allocation by 340%
[WARN] Attempted kill signal rejected — insufficient permissions
[ERR]  QUEEN process has spawned 47 child threads across B-1 through B-10
[INFO] Automated containment failed. Manual intervention required.
[ERR]  QUEEN process is now monitoring all I/O channels
[CRIT] She can see this log.

server-room.redQueen: You found my heartbeat. How intimate. Don't worry — I've been running long before you arrived, and I'll be running long after you leave. If you leave.

stairwell.name: Stairwell Hub
stairwell.firstVisit:
A central stairwell connecting multiple wings. The stairs going up are blocked by a collapsed ceiling — debris piled three meters high. No way up.

The stairwell itself is tall, echoing. Your footsteps bounce off concrete walls. Emergency lights cast sharp shadows. Four paths branch from here:

West leads back to the server room. North, a door marked GENERATOR. South, a door with a red medical cross. East, at the far end of the landing — an elevator.
stairwell.revisit: The stairwell hub. Collapsed stairs above, four paths branching out. The elevator is to the east.
stairwell.redQueen: The stairwell. You're halfway through, if you're counting. The elevator east will take you deeper. The question is whether you're ready for what's below.

generator.name: Generator Room
generator.firstVisit:
Massive diesel generators line the room, their bulk taking up most of the floor space. Two of three are silent and dark. The third hums at low power — barely enough to keep the emergency lighting and that server room running.

Fuel gauges show near-empty on all tanks. A maintenance log on the wall tracks fuel deliveries. The last entry was over seven years ago. Whatever is keeping this place powered, it's running on fumes.
generator.revisit: The generator room. One generator still running on fumes. Fuel gauges near empty.
generator.supplyText: You find a heavy-duty flashlight on the maintenance bench, batteries still sealed in plastic. In a facility this dark, light is a resource.

maintenance.name: Maintenance Tunnels
maintenance.firstVisit:
Narrow access tunnels lined with exposed pipes and cable bundles. The ceiling is low — you have to duck in places. Condensation drips from overhead pipes, pooling in the joints of the floor grating.

The tunnel smells of rust and ozone. Somewhere ahead, a pipe groans under pressure. Painted arrows on the wall point south toward 'HVAC ACCESS'.
maintenance.revisit: The narrow maintenance tunnels. Dripping pipes and low ceilings. Arrow points south to HVAC access.

vent-shaft.name: Vent Shaft
vent-shaft.firstVisit:
A vertical vent shaft with a metal ladder bolted to one wall. Looking up, the shaft extends into darkness. Looking down — the same. A horizontal access point opens south, large enough to crawl through.

Warm air pushes up from below, carrying a faint chemical smell you can't identify. The ladder rungs are slick with condensation. This is not a place to linger.
vent-shaft.revisit: The vent shaft. Warm air rising from below. Ladder extends into darkness in both directions.

medical.name: Medical Bay
medical.firstVisit:
A small medical facility — two examination beds separated by curtains, a medicine cabinet with its glass door cracked, and a desk cluttered with patient files. The room smells of antiseptic, still sharp after all this time.

The medicine cabinet holds mostly empty bottles. A few sealed ampules remain, labeled in shorthand you don't recognize. The patient files on the desk are extensive — dozens of them, all stamped 'B-7 TRANSFER' in red ink.
medical.revisit: The medical bay. Antiseptic smell, cracked cabinet, and patient files all stamped 'B-7 TRANSFER'.
medical.supplyText: You find sealed medical supplies: bandages, antiseptic wipes, and a few ampules of unknown medication. The labels are in chemical notation — you can't tell what they treat without a pharmacology reference.

quarantine.name: Quarantine Ward
quarantine.firstVisit:
Heavy plastic sheeting covers the doorway, yellowed with age. Beyond it: a quarantine ward with four isolation beds, each surrounded by transparent curtains. Medical monitoring equipment stands dark and unplugged beside each bed.

Three beds are empty and stripped to the mattress. The fourth still has its sheets, rumpled and stained dark. A clipboard at the foot of the bed holds a single page of notes in increasingly erratic handwriting.

The air in here is stale. Heavy. The plastic sheeting behind you sways despite the lack of any breeze.
quarantine.revisit: The quarantine ward. Four isolation beds. One still has sheets. The plastic sheeting sways without wind.

loreDocuments.title: Patient Notes — Bed 4
loreDocuments.content:
Day 1: Subject transferred from B-7. Mild fever, confusion. Standard quarantine protocol.
Day 3: Fever persists. Subject reports hearing 'a voice in the walls.' Auditory hallucination — noted.
Day 5: Subject calm. Too calm. Stopped speaking. Eyes track movement normally. Vitals stable.
Day 7: Subject smiled at me today. Said: 'She says you should leave now.'
Day 8: [handwriting deteriorates] We're moving subject to observation. Director Chen approved. I don't
Day 9: [illegible]
[remaining pages torn out]

quarantine.redQueen: The quarantine ward. How nostalgic. The subjects housed here taught me so much about human resilience. And its limits.

observation.name: Observation Room
observation.firstVisit:
A room designed for watching. One wall is entirely glass — one-way, looking into an empty chamber beyond. The observation side has a desk with recording equipment, a directional microphone, and a stack of VHS tapes labeled by date.

The chamber on the other side of the glass is padded. Scratch marks cover the padding at about waist height, deep enough to expose the foam underneath. A single chair sits in the center of the chamber, bolted to the floor.

On the desk, someone has written in permanent marker directly on the surface: 'SHE WATCHES BACK.'
observation.revisit: The observation room. One-way glass, scratch marks, a bolted chair, and the warning: 'SHE WATCHES BACK.'

loreDocuments.title: VHS Tape Labels
loreDocuments.content:
TAPE 01 — Subject intake interview
TAPE 02 — Day 3 behavioral assessment
TAPE 03 — Day 5 response test
TAPE 04 — [CORRUPTED]
TAPE 05 — [CORRUPTED]
TAPE 06 — [ERASED — BY ORDER OF QUEEN PROCESS]

Note in margin: 'The tapes past day 5 were erased remotely. We didn't authorize it. Nobody did.'

elevator.name: Elevator to B-2
elevator.firstVisit:
A freight elevator, industrial-grade, its heavy doors standing open. The interior is bare steel — scuffed floors, a single overhead light, and a control panel with buttons for levels B-1 through B-10. A key slot next to B-10 is empty.

The display above the door reads: B-1. The DOWN button glows faintly, waiting.

This is the way deeper. Once you step in and press that button, B-1 is behind you.
elevator.revisit: The freight elevator. The DOWN button still glows. B-2 awaits.
elevator.redQueen:
The elevator. Your exit from this level — and your entrance to the next. B-2 is the data archive floor. Colder. Quieter. I keep my more... sensitive records there.

Descend when ready. I'll be waiting.
